items.title: US 10 year yield tops 5% | AI stocks slide after slowdown calls| Coforge in focus | Opening Bell
items.summary: US indices slid 0.3-0.5% amid inflation and AI-related concerns, while Brent crude touched $109 a barrel after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline. Reports also indicated that the Houthis took control of Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, adding to concerns over global oil supplies and shipping routes. US August CPI rose 3.4% year-on-year, in line with estimates, while the 10-year Treasury yield touched 5% on Monday before retreating slightly. CME FedWatch indicated a 90% probability of a Fed rate hike this week. Global technology stocks were rattled by developments around AI, with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calling for a slower pace of AI development in a blog post, a position supported by Sam Altman and Elon Musk. Altman also said an OpenAI IPO this year would be “ill advised.” Chip and semiconductor stocks came under pressure, with Micron falling 5.25%, AMD 4.4%, Broadcom 4.8%, Marvell 7.3%, Nvidia 3.3% and ARM Holdings 9.7%. In contrast, cybersecurity stocks such as CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks surged 13-15%. Asian markets traded mixed, while Gift Nifty indicated a mildly positive start for Indian equities. The Indian market ended its fifth straight week of losses, marking its longest losing streak in 14 months. The Sensex and Nifty fell around 2% each last week, while the Midcap index declined 1%. The Nifty recovered from Friday’s lows to close at 23,398. FIIs remained net sellers, offloading ₹930.90 crore of equities, while DIIs were net buyers with purchases worth ₹1,968.17 crore. On the domestic inflation front, August CPI inflation came in above estimates at 4.82% versus 4.45% previously, while core CPI rose to 4.2% from 3.9%. August WPI inflation stood at 9.92% versus 9.78%, food inflation rose to 7.05% from 6.65%, and fuel and power inflation increased to 22.93% from 20.05%.

items.title: IPO STREET: RENTOMOJO, ARCIL, MANIPAL PAYMENTS & KARAMTARA — DECODED BY MONEYCONTROL RESEARCH
items.summary: India's IPO market is witnessing intense action, with 81 companies having already raised over Rs 83,000 crore by going public so far this year, a number set to grow further with NSE set to launch its much-awaited public issue next week. The week of September 7 to 11 saw frenzied primary market activity, with as many as 12 IPOs launched over the past five days, four of which are still open for subscription. On today's IPO Street, we take stock of these four companies gearing up to begin their listed market journey. In focus is Rentomojo, a well-known furniture and appliance rental solutions company; ARCIL, or Asset Reconstruction Company of India Limited, a financial giant that looks to generate returns by turning around distressed and bad loan assets; Manipal Payments and Identity Solutions, a Manipal Group company that manufactures debit and credit cards, offers secure payment solutions, and also operates in the government ID ecosystem, producing documents like voter cards and driving licenses; and Karamtara Engineering, a niche engineering company manufacturing key products and components for the power transmission and renewable energy sectors. To make sense of these four new listings, Moneycontrol's research team joins the show to break down the issue details, business fundamentals, financials and valuation, and their view on each offering.

items.title: Brent surges 5% to $107 | Houthis hit Saudi oil pipeline | Nifty to see gap down opening
items.summary: US markets declined for the fourth consecutive session, with the Nasdaq, Dow and S&P 500 falling around 0.5%. Brent crude surged 5.6% overnight to near $108 a barrel amid reports that Houthi rebels attacked Saudi Arabia’s East-West Oil Pipeline and seized control of Yemen’s port city of Mocha. Rising oil prices pushed US Treasury yields higher, with the 10-year yield jumping 11 basis points to 4.95%, the 2-year yield rising 13 basis points to 4.56%, its highest since July 2024, and the 30-year yield climbing to 5.34%, its highest since June 2007. Chip stocks such as Intel and Micron fell 4-6% on rate-hike concerns, while Apple gained 3.6% following the launch of its first foldable smartphone. US August Producer Price Index inflation rose 0.4% month-on-month and 5.4% year-on-year. Asian markets traded weak, with Gift Nifty indicating a gap-down opening for Indian equities. In India, the market adjusted higher following the CAS mechanism, with the Nifty ending its three-day losing streak. The Nifty saw a CAS adjustment of nearly 100 points, while the Sensex was adjusted by nearly 300 points. At 3:15 pm, the Nifty stood at 23,389 before closing at 23,478, while the Nifty Bank was at 56,262 before closing at 56,472. The Sensex stood at 74,630 at 3:15 pm and closed at 74,903. SEBI Chairman said the determination of the closing price based on CAS for derivatives on expiry day is being reworked, while noting that initial liquidity after the CAS rollout has been an issue and liquidity typically builds over time. FIIs remained net sellers, offloading ₹438.24 crore in equities, while DIIs were net buyers with purchases worth ₹1,025.85 crore. The rupee weakened to close at 95.44 per dollar, compared with Wednesday’s close of 95.11

items.title: Live: Choppy day for markets, oil above $92; Rupee recovers to 94.8/$ | Closing Bell
items.summary: Indian equity markets remained under pressure, with the Sensex falling 200 points and the Nifty slipping below the 24,000 mark. Market breadth weakened further as declines outpaced advances, while most sectoral indices traded lower. FMCG and IT stocks emerged as relative outperformers in an otherwise choppy session. Auto stocks declined following the release of August monthly sales data, adding to the broader market pressure. The Nifty Midcap index snapped its two-day winning streak, while the Nifty Smallcap index extended its losses for another session. In commodities, Brent crude climbed back above $92 per barrel, keeping investors cautious amid ongoing global uncertainties. The rupee, however, recovered 28 paise to trade at 94.8 against the US dollar. Among Nifty 50 stocks, ITC, HCL Technologies and Adani Ports were the top gainers, while Shriram Finance, Maruti Suzuki and InterGlobe Aviation featured among the biggest losers.
